title: Il mio racconto: la mia giornata
summary: Week 2 capstone: numbers, time, and the verb engine, then extend your self-intro with your daily routine

blocks.title: Uno sguardo indietro: settimana 2
blocks.body: This week you built the **verb engine**: numbers 0-100, telling time, the days and months, and three whole families of present-tense verbs — **-are** (parlo), **-ere** (leggo), and **-ire** (dormo / capisco) — plus the irregular trio **fare, andare, stare** that runs daily life. Big week. Time to put it all together.
blocks.callout: Everything from Week 3 on assumes these verb endings are second nature.

items.en: I understand a bit of Italian.

blocks.prompt: Which is the correct way to write 28?
blocks.explain: **ventotto** — venti drops its final i before otto, the same trick as ventuno.

blocks.prompt: You want the total bill at the bar. What do you ask?
blocks.explain: **Quant'è?** asks for the whole total; quanto costa is for pricing one item.

blocks.prompt: Type 'it's half past seven' in Italian.

blocks.title: Un verbo speciale: mi sveglio
blocks.body: One more verb for your toolkit, a little ahead of schedule: **svegliarsi** (to wake up) is a **reflexive** verb — it comes with a small extra word (*mi, ti, si...*) because the action reflects back on you. For now, just memorize the io-form as a fixed phrase: **mi sveglio** (I wake up), usually with a time: *mi sveglio **alle** sette e mezza*. You'll meet the whole reflexive family properly later — this one gets you talking about your day today.
blocks.callout: mi sveglio alle... — bank this phrase whole for now; the grammar behind it comes later.

items.en: I study Italian in the evening.
I go to bed at midnight.

pairs.note: Different families, same job: the ending tells you who.

blocks.speak: Mi sveglio alle sette e mezza.

mi sveglio alle sette e mezza.

blocks.scene: Marco asks about your daily routine at the bar.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.nl: Allora, com'è una tua giornata tipica?
lines.en: So, what's a typical day of yours like?

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Mi sveglio alle sette, faccio colazione e vado al lavoro.
lines.en: I wake up at seven, have breakfast, and go to work.
lines.spotlight: Three verbs, three families — sveglio, faccio, vado — all in one breath.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.nl: E la sera? Studi ancora l'italiano?
lines.en: And in the evening? Do you still study Italian?

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Sì, studio un po' e poi guardo la tv.
lines.en: Yes, I study a bit and then I watch TV.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.nl: Bravo, dai! Vai a letto presto o tardi?
lines.en: Nice, come on! Do you go to bed early or late?

lines.speaker: You
lines.en: I go to bed around midnight.

questions.q: What does 'You' do before going to work?
